analysis:
The supplied units are BASE text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-801). The PR change is documentation-only. Per file_changes, the head diff rewrites the Nemotron Super eviction and load-gate paragraph (base lines 404-407, head 404-413) and adds a section at head ~1095-1115 on parked free 64 MiB paged-KV segments. That section is parked per pool up to min(2 GiB, grant/8) outside the grant, floor and ledger charge, and is reinstalled on the next admission of the same size class. The patch excerpt is truncated and the head text is not supplied, so the segment-parking behavior is only partly visible.

Security-relevant observations:
1. Documented parking of freed KV segments could relate to T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory). The excerpt says new segments are "zero-fil...", which suggests zero-fill, but the excerpt is cut off. Whether reinstalled parked segments are scrubbed or reused across requests or tenants is not visible and cannot be verified from this doc-only diff. No source code is changed here, so I report no finding.
2. Memory parked outside the ledger charge (max 2 GiB or grant/8) is a potential unaccounted-memory/DoS consideration for the admission ledger. The doc says it is released by `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad` before eviction or refusal, which is consistent with availability controls. That implementation is not supplied.
3. The eviction and pre-accept changes are described as load-gate and availability behavior only. They have no trust-boundary, authorization, attestation or encryption impact visible here. The prefix cache (T-041) text in this file is unchanged: cache scope remains partitioned by authenticated tenant scope, and the managed slot emits no cache receipts.

No code is changed in the supplied units, so no regression or new attack surface is established. A reviewer of the accompanying source changes (the paged KV segment pool, `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad`) should confirm that parked segments are zeroed or never exposed across cache scopes (T-028) and that the unledgered parked memory is bounded.
